title: Comparators and Equality
summary: Lists the comparison operators usable in conditions and explains the difference between strict (===) and loose (==) equality using a number versus a numeric string.

concepts.heading: Comparison operators
points: === is true when both sides are equal; !== is true when they differ.
> and < test greater than and less than; >= and <= also accept equality.
Each yields a boolean, which if/else statements use to decide the branch.

concepts.heading: === versus ==
points: With a = 1 and b = "1", typeof a is "number" and typeof b is "string".
a === b is false because strict equality compares the data types as well as the values.
a == b is true because loose equality ignores type and converts first.
(Extra) Prefer === and !== by default to avoid type-coercion surprises (0 == "" is true, for example).

concepts.heading: Looking ahead
points: To give the love calculator separate messages for low, middle and high scores, comparators must be combined, which the next lecture covers.

code_examples.caption: Strict vs loose equality
Reference-repo checks
code_examples.code:
console.log(5 === "5");  // false
console.log(5 !== "5");  // true
console.log(10 >= 10);   // true
console.log(10 < 5);     // false

pitfalls: Using == and silently matching values of different types.
Mixing up > with >= at range boundaries.

playground.coverage: Covers all operators, == vs ===, the notorious loose results and the assignment pitfall. More than the lecture.
gaps_and_ideas: Add typeof a / typeof b to the task, as the lecture does.
Interactive demo idea: two inputs and an operator dropdown showing the boolean result.
